name: Amoxicillin
risk: PCN allergy; rash in EBV; diarrhea. 1st-line: otitis media, strep pharyngitis, CAP, sinusitis.

name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate
risk: Diarrhea (clav); cholestatic hepatitis. 1st-line: human/animal bite, sinusitis with risk factors, aspiration pneumonia.

name: Azithromycin
risk: QT prolongation; hepatotoxicity; GI. Use for atypical CAP, pertussis, chlamydia 1g single dose.

name: Doxycycline
risk: Photosensitivity; esophagitis (take upright); teeth staining <8y. 1st-line: CAP, Lyme, acne, chlamydia alt.

name: Ciprofloxacin
risk: Tendon rupture (esp. Achilles, >60y, steroid co-use); QT; C. diff; aortic dissection. Reserve for complicated UTI/pyelonephritis.

name: Nitrofurantoin
risk: Pulmonary fibrosis (chronic use); peripheral neuropathy; hemolysis in G6PD. 1st-line: uncomplicated cystitis.

name: TMP-SMX
risk: Hyperkalemia; SJS; ↑INR with warfarin; bone marrow. Alt 1st-line cystitis; PJP prophylaxis.

name: Cephalexin
risk: Cross-reactivity with PCN <2%. 1st-line: cellulitis, strep alternative, UTI in pregnancy.

name: Clindamycin
risk: C. diff colitis (highest risk). Used for MRSA skin, dental, severe PCN allergy.

name: Metronidazole
risk: Disulfiram reaction with alcohol; metallic taste; peripheral neuropathy. Use for BV, trichomoniasis, C. diff, anaerobes.

name: Penicillin V
risk: PCN allergy. 1st-line: strep pharyngitis, mild skin.

name: Metformin
risk: Lactic acidosis risk in renal failure/sepsis; GI intolerance; B12 deficiency (long-term). 1st-line T2DM.

name: Empagliflozin
risk: Genital mycotic infection; euglycemic DKA (hold before surgery); Fournier gangrene. CV & renal protection in T2DM + CKD/HF.
renal: eGFR <20: avoid initiation; continue down to 20

name: Dulaglutide
risk: Nausea/vomiting; pancreatitis; medullary thyroid Ca (contraindicated MEN2/MTC fh); weight loss. Weekly SC.

name: Insulin Glargine
risk: Hypoglycemia; weight gain. Start 10U or 0.1–0.2 U/kg QHS; titrate FBG 80–130.
preg: B — OK (NPH preferred historically; glargine used)

name: Glibenclamide
risk: Hypoglycemia (prolonged, esp. elderly/CKD); weight gain. Avoid elderly — prefer gliclazide.

name: Atorvastatin
risk: Myalgia; rhabdomyolysis (rare); transaminitis; new DM. No dose adjustment in mild renal.

name: Rosuvastatin
risk: Most potent statin; myalgia; transaminitis. Lower Asian dosing.

name: Ezetimibe
risk: Add-on to statin; myalgia (mild). LDL ↓18–25%.

name: Amlodipine
risk: Peripheral edema (dose-dep, up to 25%); flushing; gingival hyperplasia. 1st-line HTN, esp. Black/elderly, isolated systolic.

name: Losartan
risk: Hyperkalemia; AKI if volume-depleted/bilateral RAS; angioedema (rare vs ACEi). 1st-line HTN, HF, CKD, DM+proteinuria.

name: Ramipril
risk: Cough (~10–15%); angioedema (higher in Black, smokers); hyperkalemia; AKI. 1st-line HTN, HF, post-MI, CKD proteinuric.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
risk: Hyponatremia (esp. elderly women); hypokalemia; hyperuricemia/gout; hypercalcemia; ↑glucose; photosensitivity/SCC risk. 1st-line HTN.

name: Bisoprolol
risk: Bradycardia; AV block; fatigue; masks hypoglycemia; bronchospasm (less than non-selective). HF mortality benefit; AFib rate control.

name: Spironolactone
risk: Hyperkalemia (esp. + ACEi/ARB); gynecomastia; menstrual irregularity. HF w/ reduced EF; resistant HTN; PCOS acne/hirsutism.

name: Warfarin
risk: Bleeding; skin necrosis; teratogenic. HUGE drug/food interactions (vit K, abx, amiodarone). Target INR 2–3 (AFib/VTE); 2.5–3.5 (mech valve).

name: Apixaban
risk: Bleeding; no routine monitoring. Preferred DOAC in CKD. Dose reduce 2.5 mg BID if any 2: age ≥80, wt ≤60 kg, Cr ≥1.5.
renal: Usable down to CrCl 15–25 with caution

name: Rivaroxaban
risk: Bleeding; take with food (15 mg, 20 mg). Avoid CrCl <30.

name: Aspirin (low-dose)
risk: GI bleed; hemorrhagic stroke. Secondary prevention: strong benefit. Primary prevention: USPSTF 2022 → individualize 40–59, AVOID ≥60 de novo.
preg: Low-dose OK for preeclampsia prevention 12–36 wk in high-risk

name: Clopidogrel
risk: Bleeding; CYP2C19 variability (↓effect). Post-stent, recent ACS, stroke.

name: Fluoxetine
risk: Long half-life (safe if missed dose, hard washout for switching); activating — AM dosing; SIADH; sexual SE; first-trimester cardiac malformation small risk.
preg: C — often continued if severe depression

name: Sertraline
risk: GI SE; sexual SE; SIADH. Preferred SSRI in pregnancy/lactation. 1st-line for MDD, GAD, PTSD, panic.

name: Escitalopram
risk: QT prolongation (dose-dep, max 10 mg >65y); GI; sexual SE. 1st-line MDD, GAD.

name: Mirtazapine
risk: Sedation; weight gain; ↓anxiety; rare agranulocytosis. Good for depression + insomnia + weight loss in elderly.

name: Venlafaxine
risk: Dose-dep HTN; discontinuation syndrome (worst). MDD, GAD, neuropathic pain alt.

name: Salbutamol
risk: Tachycardia; tremor; hypokalemia (high dose). Rescue + exercise premedication.

name: Budesonide-Formoterol
risk: Oral candidiasis (rinse!); dysphonia. GINA 2023: MART/SMART for asthma step 1–5 (use as both controller AND rescue).

name: Tiotropium
risk: Dry mouth; urinary retention (BPH caution); narrow-angle glaucoma. COPD; add-on severe asthma.

name: Montelukast
risk: 2020 FDA boxed warning — neuropsychiatric (agitation, sleep, suicidality, esp. adolescents). Allergic rhinitis, exercise asthma.

name: Paracetamol
risk: Hepatotoxic >4 g/d (>3 g if liver disease, alcohol, malnutrition). 1st-line pain in CKD, HF, pregnancy.

name: Ibuprofen
risk: GI bleed (add PPI if long-term + risk); AKI; CV risk (MI, stroke); HF exacerbation; ↓ACE/diuretic effect. AVOID: CKD, HF, 3rd trimester pregnancy, age >75 chronic.

name: Naproxen
risk: Same class risks; slightly less CV risk than other NSAIDs per meta-analyses. Gout, dysmenorrhea, MSK.

name: Omeprazole
risk: Long-term: B12/Mg/Ca deficiency; ↑C. diff; interstitial nephritis; hip fracture (osteoporosis); ↓clopidogrel effect (prefer pantoprazole).

name: Levothyroxine
risk: Take fasting 30–60 min before food; separate from Ca, Fe, PPI, soy. Start low in elderly/CAD. Overreplacement → AF, osteoporosis.
preg: A — dose ↑~30% in 1st trim; target TSH <2.5

name: Colchicine
risk: GI; myopathy; bone marrow. Reduce with CKD, CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors (macrolides, statins, diltiazem). Acute gout: 1.2 mg then 0.6 mg 1h later.

name: Allopurinol
risk: HLA-B*58:01 → SJS/DRESS (screen Han Chinese, Thai, Korean). Start low (100 mg), titrate to urate <6 mg/dL. Renal dose in CKD.

name: Dipyrone (Metamizole)
risk: Rare agranulocytosis (why banned US/UK); hypotension IV. Widely used in Israel for pain, fever, colic.
